clue.text: Align new setting of this garnet

indicators.note: a new setting puts the stone's letters into a fresh arrangement, so the two words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeweller plans to line up a garnet in a new mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new setting of' rearranges the ten letters of THIS GARNET.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to put them in a true line, making them level and not crooked.

clue.text: Volatile centre of international discussions?

explanation.surface: A shaky situation at the heart of world diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as UN'S TABLE: the United Nations' table is where international discussions are held.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatile means liable to change suddenly; the UN's table is, punningly, the place where nations talk.

clue.text: Be laudatory about power to get increase in pay

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
a raise is a rise in salary, the American term

explanation.surface: A worker gets more money and can't stop speaking well of the bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: To be laudatory is to speak with admiration, which is to commend or extol.

clue.text: Garden boundary's not hard limit

indicators.note: 'not hard' tells the solver to take away the letter standing for hard

parts.note: a hedge is a row of bushes forming the boundary of a garden
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A garden's boundary isn't a firm limit at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is the outer limit or border of something.

clue.text: Our bellies, upset, refusing to behave?

indicators.note: an upset stomach is churned up, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Our stomachs are upset and refuse to settle down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the ten letters of OUR BELLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone defiant who will not obey or conform is refusing to behave.

clue.text: With some aloofness, pick dessert?

parts.note: ice is coldness of manner, as in 'an icy reception'
the pick of something is its cream, the best part

explanation.surface: A rather standoffish diner chooses what to eat after the main course.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen sweetened dairy served at the end of a meal is a popular sweet course.

clue.text: Stuff produced is not in place

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: Goods made at a factory are not where they should be.
explanation.definitionFit: Output is the quantity of goods made by a worker, machine or factory.

clue.text: Study money, having at first lost billions

indicators.note: the first letter is taken away, the letter for billions

parts.note: bread is slang for money
B is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: Looking into finances after billions were lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject at university is to study it, as in 'she read law'.

clue.text: Card game linked to the fashionable world in town

parts.note: the ton (from French 'bon ton') is old slang for fashionable society
bridge is a partnership card game

explanation.surface: Card players mingle with high society somewhere in the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: TONBRIDGE is a market town in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonbridge is a Kentish market town, a specific example of the broader category.

clue.text: It brings about legal action involving University

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A lawsuit against a university triggers events.
explanation.definitionFit: A cause is whatever produces an effect or result.

clue.text: A fixed gaze taking in one film star

indicators.note: taking in means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a stare is a long fixed look
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fan stares fixedly at a screen idol.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred ASTAIRE was the dancing Hollywood star of Top Hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was a famous Hollywood actor and dancer, an example of a screen celebrity.

clue.text: Last couple of superheroes, dressed like Batman, fled

indicators.note: the last couple of letters of the word are taken, its final two

parts.note: Batman wears a cape, so he is caped

explanation.surface: A pair of costumed crime-fighters made a getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away, so having got away means having fled.

clue.text: Film star's book involved in storm

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: a gale is a violent wind, a storm

explanation.surface: An actor's memoir is caught up in a media storm.
explanation.walkthrough: Clark GABLE starred in Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was a leading Hollywood actor, an example of a screen celebrity.

clue.text: One goes to fetch pass given to reader

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a lector is a reader, especially of lessons in church

explanation.surface: Someone is sent to pick up a mountain pass for a reader.
explanation.definitionFit: A collector gathers things in, such as a debt collector going round to fetch money.

clue.text: Appropriate, once fact is recollected

indicators.note: read as re-collected, the letters are gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: It is fitting, once a fact is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' rearranges ONCE FACT IS. 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take something for one's own use, as officials seize goods.

clue.text: Additional comment about economic situation initially prompting rethink

indicators.note: about means around, so the rider wraps round the inner pieces

parts.note: a rider is an added clause or comment
econ is a common short form of economic

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A postscript on the economy prompts a change of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ECON plus S inside RIDER after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider something is to think it over again, perhaps changing one's mind.

clue.text: production

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is only 'production (3,5,2,5)': the rest of the clue is missing and no source found it.

clue.text: Complete rustic view following on the next page

parts.note: over means finished, complete
a lea is a meadow, a country scene in poetry
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A whole countryside panorama spreads onto the next page.
explanation.definitionFit: Overleaf means on the other side of the page, so continued further on.

clue.text: Iron case melted down, as plan projected

indicators.note: metal melted down is recast, so these letters are recast in a new order

explanation.surface: An iron casing is smelted as part of a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an imagined sequence of events, a projected outline of what may happen.

clue.text: New weapon factories not initially places of seclusion?

indicators.note: not initially means without its first letter

parts.note: gunneries are taken as places where guns are made

explanation.surface: New arms plants are not at first secluded places.
explanation.definitionFit: Convents where religious women live apart from the world are places of retreat.

clue.text: Standard article describing some of the French?

parts.note: a norm is a standard
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A typical essay discusses part of the French people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans came from Normandy, a region of France, so they are some French people.

clue.text: Woman's finish mostly a glossy finish?

parts.note: she stands for a woman

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A woman's nail varnish ends up mostly shiny.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin SHEEN, father of Charlie, is the film star of this puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrous shine on a surface is a glossy finish.

clue.text: African native thus linked to African country

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A person from one African land has ties to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalis are the people of Somalia in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: A keen taste, for the most part, in modern kind of painting

parts.note: to keen is to wail, so a keen is a cry

indicators.note: for the most part means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a lick is a taste with the tongue

explanation.surface: Someone with a sharp palate tries a contemporary picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint made with synthetic resin is a twentieth-century medium for artists.

clue.text: Opponent cannot win, having ignored all the odds

indicators.note: ignoring the odd letters leaves only the even ones, the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A rival can't succeed when the odds are stacked against them.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is someone against a proposal, an opposer.

annotationWithheld.clue: Reduced tempo reduced anxiety in orchestra members

clue.text: Drop in rent?

explanation.surface: A small reduction in what a tenant pays.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear is a drop shed from the eye, and a tear is also a rip or rent in cloth.

clue.text: Crown, one found in royal Irish location

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside another piece

parts.note: the Hill of Tara in County Meath was the seat of the ancient High Kings of Ireland
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A crown discovered at an ancient Irish royal site.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled headband, a kind of coronet.

clue.text: Off-road transport a bit like scrambling? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the inner piece
scrambling mixes things up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Motorbike scrambling over rough ground, fair enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambling' rearranges A BIT LIKE into TAILBIKE; 'about' puts R inside, after the T. Scrambling is also motorcycle racing over rough terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: A light motorcycle built for rough tracks and dirt is a vehicle for use away from roads.
